text: How should Lakeshore explain the value of AbarVa versus a manual consulting assessment?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Lakeshore Holdings should frame AbarVa's value as a living decision substrate, not a one-time diligence artifact — the difference between a PDF that ages the moment it's delivered and an always-on tenant graph that keeps pace with your portfolio. Three specific arguments hold up for Lakeshore.
First, continuity: a manual consulting assessment freezes a view of your 68 in-scope data sources, your Finance AI variance-explainer initiative (design stage, $7M budget against $17M promised benefit, target 2026-12-15), and payment straight-through-processing at 58% against a 92% target. Those numbers move.
AbarVa re-grounds against the loaded tenant chunks every turn, so the CFO isn't rereading a stale deck when a design-stage initiative slips or an STP metric shifts. Second, cost and speed geometry. 5–3M spend over 10–14 weeks, delivered as slides.
AbarVa delivers the same synthesis conversationally, on demand, against your actual initiative ledger, KPI dictionary, and evidence rows — with the reasoning auditable turn by turn. Third, decision fidelity.
Consultants generalize from prior engagements; AbarVa grounds in Lakeshore's own governed-metric dependencies, owner roles (Treasurer for STP, CFO for the Finance AI expansion), and source-readiness constraints before recommending automation. That's a materially different quality of advice for a diversified holdco where each operating company has its own data substrate.
The honest caveat: consultants still win on deep interview-driven cultural diagnostics and on physical-presence change management.
